issues.body: `route_post` decides that a body is a handshake solely from its method/id shape, dispatches it, and then creates a session whenever `handle_message` returns any response. It never verifies that the response is a successful initialize result. Thus an initialize request with invalid JSON-RPC metadata or invalid initialize parameters can receive an error object while still getting `Mcp-Session-Id`; subsequent calls with that ID pass the session check. This contradicts the documented "successful handshake mints one" lifecycle and admits clients that never completed initialization.
issues.fix_hint: Mint only after confirming the initialize dispatch produced a successful JSON-RPC result for the admitted initialize request (not an error response). Prefer exposing a typed dispatch outcome rather than heuristically inspecting arbitrary serialized JSON. Add a regression test that sends an invalid initialize request, asserts the error response has no `mcp-session-id`, asserts `session_count() == 0`, and proves the would-be session cannot make a later request.
issues.title: Failed initialize requests can mint live sessions

issues.body: `read_request` stores every header but `lookup("content-length")` selects only the first value. A request containing multiple different Content-Length fields is therefore parsed using whichever value appears first, while an upstream proxy may reject it, combine it, or choose another value. That disagreement is a classic HTTP request-framing ambiguity; closing the backend connection reduces some exploitation shapes but does not make ambiguous framing safe behind intermediaries. The module explicitly claims to refuse rather than guess on smuggling-sensitive framing, so accepting this case also violates its stated invariant.
issues.fix_hint: Collect all Content-Length occurrences before reading the body. Reject multiple fields unless every parsed value is identical (the safest small-server policy is to reject any duplicate), reject comma-joined/malformed forms, and keep rejecting every Transfer-Encoding occurrence. Add parser tests for conflicting duplicates and duplicate-equal fields that pin the chosen policy.
issues.title: Conflicting duplicate Content-Length headers are accepted

verdict.summary: The transport is thoughtfully bounded and well tested, but two correctness/security gaps remain in load-bearing protocol paths. A syntactically classified initialize request mints a session whenever dispatch returns any JSON-RPC response, including an error response, so unsuccessful initialization can create a live session. The HTTP parser also accepts conflicting duplicate Content-Length fields and uses the first one, leaving an avoidable request-framing ambiguity at proxy boundaries. Both require fixes and focused regression tests before approval.
